mechanism_of_action: Novel, orally bioavailable small molecule with anti-inflammatory activity.
primary_endpoint: Mean change from baseline in cholesterol efflux capacity at 12 weeks and triglyceride levels at 8 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Open-label arm: cholesterol efflux capacity changed by −0.013 at 12 weeks; triglycerides changed by −21.67 mg/dL at 8 weeks. No comparator or statistical significance was reported.
safety_signal: No serious adverse events among 19 participants; no deaths.

primary_endpoint: Histological improvement, clinical improvement, and change in hepatic gene expression (2 hours after oral 75 g glucose load), assessed at 30 weeks.

mechanism_of_action: Glucagon/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor dual agonist.
primary_endpoint: Single-dose cohorts: AUC from 0 to infinity and Cmax. Multiple-dose cohorts: drug-related treatment-emergent adverse events.
efficacy_outcome: After 28 weeks, liver fat content, liver stiffness, liver volume, body weight, and other hepatic and metabolic markers were generally reduced; no numerical estimates or comparator were reported.
safety_signal: Drug-related adverse events occurred in 25.0% of healthy participants and ≤25.0% of participants with cirrhosis after single doses; rates in multiple-dose cohorts were 82.4% and 87.5%, respectively.

efficacy_outcome: At 8 weeks, versus placebo, curcumin significantly reduced CML (148 ± 108 vs 197 ± 101 ng/mL; P=0.04), 8-OHdG (46.9 ± 31.1 vs 52.1 ± 43.1 ng/mL; P=0.03), liver enzymes (P<0.001), and several anthropometric measures. It did not significantly change sRAGE, hip circumference, waist/hip ratio, or fat-free mass.

mechanism_of_action: GLP-1 agonist
primary_endpoint: Improvement in NASH at 12 months.

mechanism_of_action: Long-acting glycopegylated FGF21 analogue.
primary_endpoint: At 24 weeks: fibrosis improvement (≥1 stage) without worsening of NASH, and NASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis.
efficacy_outcome: Fibrosis improvement: 7% with placebo vs. 22%, 26%, and 27% with pegozafermin 15, 30, and 44 mg, respectively; differences were significant for 30 mg (19 percentage points; P=0.009) and 44 mg (20 percentage points; P=0.008), but not 15 mg. NASH resolution: 2% with placebo vs. 37%, 23%, and 26%, respectively; reported 95% CIs for the differences excluded zero at all doses.
safety_signal: Most common adverse events associated with pegozafermin were nausea and diarrhea.

primary_endpoint: Participants with AEs/SAEs through Day 112 and change from baseline in ALT at Day 84 (Week 12).
efficacy_outcome: ALT outcome values were 67.215 (100 mg), 48.114 (50 mg), and 59.544 (placebo); additional reported values were 0.667, 0.702, and 0.901, respectively. Reported ANCOVA p-values were 0.7489, 0.0005, and 0.0005; the registry summary does not clearly map these p-values to treatment comparisons.
safety_signal: Participants with AEs: 35 (LMB763 100 mg), 37 (50 mg), and 33 (placebo); with SAEs: 2/37, 3/44, and 0/40, respectively. No deaths were reported.

drugs.name: low carbohydrate, high protein calorie-restricted diet, exercise, and intensive dietitian counseling
balanced calorie-restricted diet, exercise, and standard counseling

primary_endpoint: Change in fat attenuation parameter (FAP) from baseline to week 12, analyzed in the per-protocol set.
efficacy_outcome: Compared with control, intensive lifestyle intervention significantly reduced FAP (LS mean difference, 16.07 dB/m; 95% CI, 8.90–23.25) and BMI (1.46 kg/m²; 95% CI, 1.09–1.82); LSM improvement was not significant (0.20 kPa; 95% CI, −0.19 to 0.59).

primary_endpoint: Resolution of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis; timepoint not reported.
efficacy_outcome: MASH resolution was 62.9% (RR 1.84, 95% CI 1.49–2.27); comparator event rate not reported.
safety_signal: No increase in psychiatric or cancer risk was observed.

primary_endpoint: Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) over 52 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Versus placebo, resmetirom 80 mg and 100 mg reduced LDL-C by 11.1% and 12.6%, apoB by 15.6% and 18.0%, triglycerides by 15.4% and 20.4%, and hepatic fat at week 16 by 34.9% and 38.6% (P < 0.0001).
safety_signal: TEAEs occurred in 86.1% (100 mg), 88.4% (80 mg), 86.5% (open-label 100 mg), and 81.8% (placebo); diarrhea and nausea exceeded placebo at treatment initiation.

primary_endpoint: Change in serum ALT and MRI-determined hepatic steatosis at 12 weeks.

mechanism_of_action: GLP-1/glucagon dual receptor agonist.
primary_endpoint: Relative reduction from baseline in liver fat content after 12 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: At week 12, liver fat content fell by 46.6%, 68.5%, and 57.1% with pemvidutide 1.2, 1.8, and 2.4 mg, respectively, versus 4.4% with placebo (p<0.001 for each dose vs. placebo).
safety_signal: Well-tolerated at all doses; no severe or serious adverse events.

mechanism_of_action: Selective thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist.
primary_endpoint: Relative liver fat reduction assessed by MRI-PDFF at week 36.
efficacy_outcome: At OLE week 36, MRI-PDFF decreased by a mean 11.1% (SE 1.5%; P < 0.0001), corresponding to a 52.3% mean relative reduction (SE 4.4%; P < 0.0001) from baseline.
safety_signal: Well tolerated, with few nonserious adverse events.

primary_endpoint: MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis or improvement in at least one fibrosis stage without worsening of MASH; liver fat reduction was also assessed.
efficacy_outcome: In MASH with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis, GLP-1RAs increased the odds of MASH resolution (OR 3.48, 95% CI 2.69–4.51) and fibrosis improvement (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.37–2.35) versus placebo. Liver fat decreased (mean difference −4.50%, 95% CI −6.60 to −2.40%); semaglutide did not improve MASH resolution or fibrosis in the single compensated-cirrhosis RCT.

mechanism_of_action: Glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue.
primary_endpoint: Proportion with improvement in liver fibrosis of at least one stage without worsening of NASH at 48 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Primary endpoint: 5/47 (11%) with semaglutide vs 7/24 (29%) with placebo; OR 0.28 (95% CI 0.06–1.24), p=0.087. NASH resolution also did not differ significantly (p=0.29).
safety_signal: Adverse events occurred in 42/47 (89%) vs 19/24 (79%); serious adverse events in 6/47 (13%) vs 2/24 (8%) with semaglutide vs placebo. Nausea (45% vs 17%), diarrhoea (19% vs 8%), and vomiting (17% vs 0%) were more common with semaglutide; no decompensating events or deaths.

mechanism_of_action: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs).
efficacy_outcome: Across 25 RCTs (2,600 patients), GLP-1RAs reduced liver fat content by 5.21% over a median 24 weeks. Histological steatosis, ballooning, and lobular inflammation improved significantly; fibrosis did not improve significantly.
safety_signal: No drug-related adverse effects involving the liver were observed.

mechanism_of_action: Modulator of the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier.
primary_endpoint: Change in HbA1c and change in the weighted average of standardized AST, CK-18, and HbA1c values from baseline to Week 26.

drugs.name: dietary supplement containing dry extracts of bergamot and artichoke

efficacy_outcome: At 12 weeks, fatty liver index improved versus placebo (p < 0.05); several NAFLD indexes also improved versus baseline.

mechanism_of_action: Not stated; the abstract notes reported anti-inflammatory and insulin-sensitizing effects.
primary_endpoint: Change in hepatic fat content and NAFLD progression after 6 months, assessed by liver biopsy.
efficacy_outcome: Compared with placebo, vitamin D significantly improved hepatic steatosis and lobular inflammation, but not hepatocyte ballooning or fibrosis. AST, ALT, TG, LDL, FBG, FBI, and HOMA-IR decreased, while vitamin D levels and HDL increased (P < 0.05).

mechanism_of_action: Alters gut microbiota composition and functionality, with changes in branched-chain amino acid availability linked to hepatic steatosis.
primary_endpoint: Intrahepatic triglyceride content (IHTC) after 4 months.
efficacy_outcome: Compared with control (n=97), RS (n=99) reduced IHTC by 9.08% (5.89% after adjustment for weight loss).

primary_endpoint: Change in transient hepatic elastography (THE) parameters from one week before surgery to three months after surgery.
efficacy_outcome: THE decreased from 8.13 to 5.53 kPa with sleeve gastrectomy versus 9.25 to 8.81 kPa with gastric bypass (between-group P=.004). CAP decreased from 287 to 242 dB/m versus 290 to 276 dB/m, respectively (P<.0001).

primary_endpoint: Highly sensitive CRP, liver fibrosis and steatosis, ALT, AST, CAP, and FAST score at six months (change from baseline).

efficacy_outcome: At 12 weeks, berberine versus placebo significantly reduced ALT (p=0.0105) and de Ritis ratio (p=0.0011); the between-group difference in change in total cholesterol favored berberine (p=0.0009). No significant differences were detected in other lipid or glucose parameters.

mechanism_of_action: Dual GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist.
primary_endpoint: Changes in HbA1c and body weight at week 14.
efficacy_outcome: Cotadutide significantly decreased HbA1c and body weight versus placebo at weeks 14 and 54 (all P < 0.001).
safety_signal: The most common adverse events with cotadutide were nausea (35%) and vomiting (17%); these decreased over time.

primary_endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: fibrosis improvement ≥1 stage without MASH worsening, and MASH resolution without worsening fibrosis.
efficacy_outcome: Across 29 RCTs (n=9,324), several therapies were significantly better than placebo on each co-primary endpoint. Pegozafermin ranked highest for fibrosis regression (SUCRA 79.92) and MASH resolution (SUCRA 91.75); survodutide and tirzepatide ranked next for resolution (SUCRA 90.87 and 84.70).

primary_endpoint: Change in controlled attenuation parameter and traditional Chinese medicine syndrome scale through study completion (average 8 weeks).

mechanism_of_action: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor.
efficacy_outcome: At 24 weeks, fatty liver grades improved, especially with ertugliflozin; Grade 2 cases decreased from 45% to 23.4% with ertugliflozin and from 41.7% to 26.6% with pioglitazone. AST and ALT decreased across groups, especially with ertugliflozin (P ≤ .001).

mechanism_of_action: Selective peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha modulator (SPPARMalpha).
primary_endpoint: Percentage change in MRI-PDFF from baseline to week 24.
efficacy_outcome: Primary endpoint: −5.3% with pemafibrate vs −4.2% with placebo (treatment difference −1.0%, P=0.85). MRE-based liver stiffness decreased versus placebo at week 48 (difference −5.7%, P=0.036) and week 72 (−6.2%, P=0.024); ALT and LDL-C also decreased significantly.
safety_signal: Adverse events were comparable between groups; therapy was well tolerated.

primary_endpoint: Changes in HbA1c, fasting glucose, body weight, BMI, BMI z scores or percentiles, BMI SDS, lipids, and blood pressure.
efficacy_outcome: GLP-1 RAs significantly reduced HbA1c (-0.44 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.68 to -0.21), fasting glucose (-9.92 mg/dL; 95% CI, -16.20 to -3.64), body weight (-3.02 kg; 95% CI, -4.98 to -1.06), BMI (-1.45; 95% CI, -2.40 to -0.49), BMI SDS (-0.20; 95% CI, -0.36 to -0.05), BMI percentile (-7.24%; 95% CI, -12.97 to -1.51), and systolic blood pressure (-2.73 mm Hg; 95% CI, -4.04 to -1.43) versus placebo.
safety_signal: Gastrointestinal adverse events increased (log rate ratio, 0.75); other adverse events, including suicidal ideation or behaviors, showed no significant differences.

primary_endpoint: Cohort 1: resolution of NASH/MASH and ≥1-stage improvement in fibrosis at 52 weeks; event-free survival at 240 weeks.

efficacy_outcome: Across the 8-week diet groups, reported changes in dietary intake were significantly correlated with liver enzymes and fatty liver index (FLI) (p<0.05); group-specific effect estimates were not provided.

mechanism_of_action: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist.
primary_endpoint: Change from baseline to week 48 in liver stiffness assessed by magnetic resonance elastography.
efficacy_outcome: Liver stiffness did not differ significantly from placebo at week 48 (estimated treatment ratio 0.96, 95% CI 0.89–1.03; P=0.2798). Liver steatosis reductions were greater with semaglutide at weeks 24, 48, and 72 (estimated treatment ratios 0.70, 0.47, and 0.50; all P≤0.0002).

Across 13 studies, steatosis grade decreased (SMD −1.73, 95% CI −2.11 to −1.35; p<0.00001) and NAS decreased (SMD −1.09, 95% CI −1.39 to −0.79; p<0.00001). Liver function tests and lipid profile also significantly improved.

mechanism_of_action: Antioxidant activity; the abstract attributes reduced systemic inflammation mainly to increased circulating IL-10 in response to DNA damage recovery.
efficacy_outcome: After four months, IL-6 decreased and IL-10 increased significantly only with HXT+VitE; 4-HNE and 8-OHdG also decreased significantly in that group. IL-1beta and TNF-alpha decreased in both groups; no effect sizes or p-values are reported.

primary_endpoint: Reduction of intrahepatic fat content measured by magnetic resonance spectroscopy at 3 months.

mechanism_of_action: Peptide co-agonist at the GLP-1 and glucagon (GCG) receptors.
efficacy_outcome: At 19 weeks, cotadutide 600 μg versus placebo reduced absolute hepatic fat fraction by 5.0 percentage points (95% CI, −8.5 to −1.5), ALT by 23.5 U/L (95% CI, −47.1 to −1.8), and AST by 16.8 U/L (95% CI, −33.0 to −0.8).
safety_signal: Any-grade treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 91.7% with 600 μg, 76.9% with 300 μg, and 37.5% with placebo; events were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal events. Discontinuations due to these events occurred in 16.7%, 7.7%, and 4.2%, respectively.

mechanism_of_action: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor.
primary_endpoint: Change in epicardial fat volume between empagliflozin and placebo from baseline to 12 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: No effect on myocardial or epicardial fat; liver fat content decreased by 27 ± 23% with empagliflozin versus 2 ± 24% with placebo (p = 0.0005).

primary_endpoint: Percentage of total body weight loss (TBWL%) at the end of the study.
efficacy_outcome: All medications produced significantly greater TBWL% than placebo (P < 0.0001); semaglutide and tirzepatide produced more than 10% TBWL. Tirzepatide was reported effective in remission of MASH, with no quantitative result provided.

primary_endpoint: Reduction in hepatic fat and stiffness measured by FibroScan, and changes in serum hepatic enzymes and CK-18 levels over 6 months.
efficacy_outcome: Neither chlorogenic acid nor caffeine was superior to placebo for hepatic fat, stiffness, or other hepatic outcomes. Compared with placebo, total cholesterol was lower with caffeine (p=0.04), and insulin was higher with chlorogenic acid plus caffeine (p=0.01); other between-group differences were not significant.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits the expression and activity of dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP4).

primary_endpoint: Change in TNF-α levels from baseline to week 12.

safety_signal: Compared with placebo, GLP-1RAs increased cholelithiasis risk (RR 1.46; 95% CI 1.09–1.97; 2 more cases per 1,000) and probably increased GERD risk (RR 2.19; 95% CI 1.48–3.25; 4 more cases per 1,000). They probably had little or no effect on other gastrointestinal or biliary events.

efficacy_outcome: Compared with controls, dapagliflozin was associated with greater decreases in liver enzymes and metabolic measures, but pooled effect estimates were not provided in the abstract.
safety_signal: No difference in adverse events between dapagliflozin and control groups; event rates were not provided.

mechanism_of_action: Liver-directed ACC1/2 inhibition; the combination also includes a DGAT2 inhibitor.
primary_endpoint: Percent change from baseline in liver fat assessed by MRI-PDFF at 16 weeks (monotherapy trial) and 6 weeks (combination trial).
efficacy_outcome: At 16 weeks, liver-fat reductions were dose-dependent with PF-05221304: −49.9%, −55.9% and −64.8% at 10, 25 and 50 mg QD, versus −7.2% with placebo. At 6 weeks, placebo-adjusted reductions were −44.6% with PF-05221304 plus PF-06865571, −44.5% with PF-05221304 alone and −35.4% with PF-06865571 alone.
safety_signal: With PF-05221304 monotherapy, serum triglycerides increased in 23/305 patients (8%), leading to withdrawal in 13/305 (4%); other serum lipids also increased dose-dependently. Combination-treatment AEs occurred in 10/28 patients (36%), with no AE-related discontinuations, and the triglyceride effect was mitigated.

mechanism_of_action: Adeno-associated virus vector-mediated fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) gene therapy.
primary_endpoint: Safety outcomes through 52 weeks; serum biomarker changes at 6 weeks; liver fat changes by MRI-PDFF and CAP at 26 weeks.
Change in liver fat content measured by ¹H-MRS at 12 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Liver fat content did not change significantly in either the prebiotic or placebo group; liver function, metabolic, and inflammatory parameters also showed no significant changes.

mechanism_of_action: PPAR pan-agonist.
primary_endpoint: Percentage change in liver fat content measured by MRI-PDFF at week 18.
efficacy_outcome: At week 18, liver fat decreased by 28.1% with chiglitazar 48 mg and 39.5% with 64 mg, versus 3.2% with placebo; differences versus placebo were 24.9% (p<0.05) and 36.3% (p<0.001), respectively.
safety_signal: Both doses were well tolerated; most adverse events were mild to moderate.

efficacy_outcome: The pooled total effective rate favored pioglitazone (8 studies; Z=3.64, 95% CI 1.31–2.43, P=.0003); several metabolic and liver enzyme measures also significantly favored treatment.

mechanism_of_action: An ionic salt of berberine and ursodeoxycholic acid.
primary_endpoint: Reduction in liver fat content measured by MRI-PDFF at 18 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: At 1000 mg twice daily, mean absolute liver-fat decrease was 4.8% versus 2.0% with placebo (p=0.011).
safety_signal: Diarrhea and abdominal discomfort were the most frequently reported adverse events.

mechanism_of_action: Liver-directed antisense inhibitor of diacylglycerol O-acyltransferase 2 (DGAT2), suppressing de novo lipogenesis.
primary_endpoint: At week 51, at least a 2-point reduction in NAS with at least a 1-point improvement in hepatocellular ballooning or lobular inflammation, without worsening of fibrosis.
efficacy_outcome: The primary endpoint was met by 18/39 (46%) with ION224 90 mg (risk difference vs placebo 27.4%, p=0.0094) and 20/34 (59%) with 120 mg (risk difference 40.1%, p=0.0002), versus 6/32 (19%) with placebo.
safety_signal: Adverse events occurred in 107 (94%) of ION224-treated participants and 41/46 (89%) receiving placebo. No deaths or treatment-related serious adverse events were reported; ION224 was described as safe and well tolerated.

primary_endpoint: Improvement in steatohepatitis from baseline to Week 48.

efficacy_outcome: Probiotics significantly reduced ALT (P=0.00001), AST (P=0.0009), GGT (P=0.04), TG (P=0.01), LDL-C (P=0.0005), HDL-C (P=0.0002), insulin (P=0.003), IR (P=0.03), BMI (P=0.03), TNF-alpha (P=0.03), and CRP (P=0.02); 1,403 participants were included.

mechanism_of_action: Selective inhibitor of apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1 (ASK1).
primary_endpoint: Proportion with ≥1-stage improvement in fibrosis without worsening of NASH at week 48.
efficacy_outcome: Neither trial met the primary endpoint. STELLAR-3: 10% (18 mg; p=0.49) and 12% (6 mg; p=0.93) vs 13% with placebo; STELLAR-4: 14% (18 mg; p=0.56) and 13% (6 mg; p=0.93) vs 13% with placebo.
safety_signal: Rates and types of adverse events were similar in selonsertib and placebo groups.

mechanism_of_action: Dual peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-alpha/gamma agonist.
primary_endpoint: Percentage change from baseline in ALT levels at week 16.
efficacy_outcome: Week-16 ALT change was −25.5%, −27.7%, and −45.8% with saroglitazar 1, 2, and 4 mg, respectively, versus +3.4% with placebo (P < 0.001 for all).
safety_signal: Saroglitazar was well tolerated; mean weight gain was 1.5 kg with 4 mg versus 0.3 kg with placebo (P = 0.27).

primary_endpoint: Comparison between pioglitazone and placebo groups in steatosis and liver function tests at 9 months; clinical safety evaluation at 9 months.

mechanism_of_action: Dual agonist of the glucagon receptor and GLP-1 receptor.
primary_endpoint: At 48 weeks, histologic improvement in MASH (reduction) with no worsening of fibrosis.
efficacy_outcome: Primary endpoint occurred in 47%, 62%, and 43% with survodutide 2.4, 4.8, and 6.0 mg, respectively, versus 14% with placebo (P<0.001 for the quadratic dose-response curve).
safety_signal: Nausea occurred in 66% vs 23%, diarrhea in 49% vs 23%, and vomiting in 41% vs 4% with survodutide versus placebo; serious adverse events occurred in 8% vs 7%.

mechanism_of_action: Described as modulating inflammation, oxidative stress, hepatic fat accumulation, and fibrosis.
primary_endpoint: Change in tumor necrosis factor (TNF) levels over 12 months.
efficacy_outcome: TNF levels were significantly lower with curcumin than placebo at all follow-up points (p < 0.001). IL-1β, IL-6, and malondialdehyde also declined, antioxidant enzyme activities increased (all p < 0.001), and hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness significantly improved versus placebo; no numerical effect sizes were reported.

mechanism_of_action: Anti-inflammatory role; the source suggests improved inflammatory cytokine levels may contribute to anti-steatotic effects.
efficacy_outcome: After 8 weeks, curcuminoids improved ultrasound-assessed NAFLD severity (p=0.002) and reduced weight versus placebo (p=0.016); TNF-alpha (p=0.024), MCP-1 (p=0.008), and EGF (p=0.0001) also improved.

mechanism_of_action: Dual agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptors.
primary_endpoint: Changes from baseline in ALT, AST, K-18, Pro-C3, and adiponectin at 26 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: At 26 weeks, tirzepatide significantly reduced ALT (all doses), AST (all except 10 mg), K-18 (5, 10, and 15 mg), and Pro-C3 (15 mg) from baseline. Versus placebo, K-18 decreased significantly with 10 mg and Pro-C3 with 15 mg; ALT decreased significantly versus dulaglutide with 10 and 15 mg. Adiponectin increased significantly versus placebo with 10 and 15 mg.

At 12 weeks, versus placebo, wheat germ significantly reduced hepatic steatosis (p=0.043), ALT (p=0.006), GGT (p=0.004), total cholesterol (p=0.018), triglycerides (p=0.046), and hs-CRP (p=0.031), and increased TAC (p=0.001).

mechanism_of_action: Long-acting Fc-FGF21 fusion protein; FGF21 is described as anti-fibrotic and as improving metabolic status.
primary_endpoint: Absolute change from baseline in hepatic fat fraction measured by MRI-PDFF at week 12.
efficacy_outcome: At week 12, HFF changed by −12.3%, −13.4%, and −14.1% with efruxifermin 28, 50, and 70 mg, respectively, versus +0.3% with placebo (P<0.0001 for each dose vs placebo).
safety_signal: Among 79 patients receiving study drug, 70 (89%) had at least one TEAE; 64 (81%) had grade 1–2, five (6%) grade 3, and one grade 4. The most common drug-related TEAEs were grade 1–2 gastrointestinal events (36; 46%).

primary_endpoint: Change in ALT from baseline to Week 12.
efficacy_outcome: Week 12 ALT ratio: 0.959 with mitiperstat 5 mg vs 0.895 with placebo; p=0.893.
safety_signal: Serious AEs affected 0/56 participants receiving treatment and 3/56 receiving placebo; no deaths in either group.

mechanism_of_action: Agonist of the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptors.
primary_endpoint: Resolution of MASH without worsening of fibrosis at 52 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Resolution occurred in 10% with placebo versus 44%, 56%, and 62% with tirzepatide 5, 10, and 15 mg, respectively (all comparisons P<0.001).

mechanism_of_action: Liver-targeted antisense oligonucleotide against PNPLA3 mRNA.
efficacy_outcome: At week 12, placebo-corrected least-square mean changes in hepatic steatosis were −7.6% with 25 mg and −12.2% with 50 mg. At 80 mg, liver PNPLA3 mRNA knockdown was 89%; the abstract also reports reduced protein levels.
safety_signal: Generally well tolerated, with no adverse events leading to discontinuation or treatment-related serious adverse events.

efficacy_outcome: Over 3 months, chromium picolinate significantly reduced TG, AIP, VLDL, insulin, HOMA-IR, hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-alpha, and fetuin-A versus placebo (p<0.05), and increased QUICKI. No significant between-group differences were reported for TC, HDL, LDL, FBS, HbA1c, or IL-17; liver steatosis intensity was unchanged.

mechanism_of_action: Pan-PPAR agonist that modulates metabolic, inflammatory, and fibrogenic pathways.
primary_endpoint: At 24 weeks, decrease of at least 2 points in SAF-A score without worsening of fibrosis.
efficacy_outcome: Primary endpoint met with lanifibranor 1200 mg vs placebo (55% vs 33%, P=0.007), but not with 800 mg (48% vs 33%, P=0.07).
safety_signal: Adverse-event dropout rate was <5% and similar across groups. Diarrhea, nausea, peripheral edema, anemia, and weight gain occurred more frequently with lanifibranor than placebo.

efficacy_outcome: The 12 g/day group had significantly reduced liver steatosis and BMI. In the 24 g/day group, liver steatosis reduction was a trend (p = 0.07); AST and total cholesterol decreased significantly (both p = 0.03).

primary_endpoint: Treatment-emergent adverse events at 12 weeks.

mechanism_of_action: Oral, liver-directed, thyroid hormone receptor beta-selective agonist.
primary_endpoint: At week 52: NASH resolution with no worsening of fibrosis, and fibrosis improvement by at least one stage with no worsening of the NAFLD activity score.
efficacy_outcome: NASH resolution: 25.9% (80 mg) and 29.9% (100 mg) vs 9.7% with placebo; fibrosis improvement: 24.2% and 25.9% vs 14.2%, respectively (P<0.001 for both doses vs placebo for both endpoints).
safety_signal: Diarrhea and nausea were more frequent with resmetirom than placebo. Serious adverse events occurred in 10.9% (80 mg), 12.7% (100 mg), and 11.5% (placebo).

mechanism_of_action: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
primary_endpoint: Change in controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) score after 24 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: At week 24, CAP was lower with dapagliflozin than control (266.3 ± 57.8 vs 298.6 ± 59.0 dB/m; p=0.002); fatty liver grade was also lower (1.7 ± 0.7 vs 2.2 ± 0.8; p<0.001).
safety_signal: No adverse events were observed.

mechanism_of_action: Modulation of gut bacterial composition.
primary_endpoint: Change in MRI-PDFF and gut microbiota composition from baseline to week 24.
efficacy_outcome: MRI-PDFF decreased significantly from week 0 to week 24 in the oligonol group; the decrease in the placebo group was not significant. No between-group statistical comparison was reported.

primary_endpoint: Access site-related major or minor vascular complications at 30 days.
efficacy_outcome: Primary endpoint: 10% with MANTA vs. 4% with ProGlide (p = 0.16). Modified VCD failure: 20% vs. 40% (p < 0.01), respectively.
safety_signal: Clinically significant access site bleeding was 9% with MANTA vs. 6% with ProGlide (p = 0.57).

mechanism_of_action: Sodium glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor.
efficacy_outcome: Hepatic fibrosis ameliorated in 70.6% (12/17) of ipragliflozin participants versus 22.2% (4/18) of controls (P < 0.01). NASH resolved in 66.7% versus 27.3%, respectively.

drugs.name: Combination of cynara scolymus, silybum marianum, curcuma longa, and glycyrrhiza glabra

primary_endpoint: MRI proton density fat fraction in hepatic steatosis, baseline to up to 12 weeks.

efficacy_outcome: IF was associated with significant improvements in ALT, AST, hepatic steatosis, and hepatic stiffness (all p<0.05); body weight, BMI, and waist-to-hip ratio also improved (p<0.05).

mechanism_of_action: N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small-interfering RNA targeting liver-expressed HSD17B13 mRNA.
primary_endpoint: Frequency of adverse events; no timepoint specified.
efficacy_outcome: In Part B, liver HSD17B13 mRNA decreased dose-dependently, with a median reduction of 78% at 6 months in the 400 mg group.
safety_signal: In Part A, injection-site reactions occurred in 11% of rapirosiran-treated participants and were mild and transient; no treatment-related serious AEs. In Part B, COVID-19 occurred in 14% (5/36) and was deemed treatment-unrelated; no drug-induced liver injury was observed.

efficacy_outcome: Across 10 trials (544 participants), vitamin D significantly reduced fasting glucose (SMD −0.22; 95% CI −0.39 to −0.04), insulin (−0.68; −1.22 to −0.14), and HOMA-IR (−1.32; −2.30 to −0.34). ALT and TAG reductions were not statistically significant; pooled effects did not support benefit for AST, TC, HDL-C, or LDL-C.

ALT decreased with pioglitazone (MD −38.41, p<0.001), SGLT2 inhibitors (−16.17, p<0.001), GLP-1 agonists (−27.98, p=0.04), and DPP-4 inhibitors (−7.41, p<0.001). Steatosis improved significantly with pioglitazone (SMD −1.01, p<0.001) and GLP-1 agonists (−2.53, p=0.03), but not significantly with SGLT2 inhibitors or DPP-4 inhibitors (p=0.06 for each).

primary_endpoint: Open-label part: improvement of fibrosis based on liver biopsy (up to 72 or 120 weeks); double-blind part: liver histology at 72 weeks and a composite long-term outcome.
efficacy_outcome: Open-label fibrosis improvement percentages reported: 31.4%, 26.5%, 51.0%, 74.5%, and 41.2%. Double-blind endpoint results are expected in 2027.
safety_signal: In the open-label part, 1/154 participants had a serious adverse event; the deaths entry is listed as “154” in the source.

efficacy_outcome: Semaglutide increased NASH resolution (OR 3.18, 95% CI 1.70–5.95; P<0.001); fibrosis stage did not significantly improve (OR 0.71, 95% CI 0.15–3.41; P=0.67).
safety_signal: GI-related side effects were more frequent with semaglutide (OR 3.72, 95% CI 1.68–8.23; P=0.001); serious adverse events were similar to placebo (OR 1.40, 95% CI 0.75–2.62).

mechanism_of_action: TERN-501 is a thyroid hormone receptor-beta (THRβ) agonist; TERN-101 is a farnesoid X receptor agonist.
primary_endpoint: Relative change from baseline at week 12 in liver fat content by MRI-PDFF with TERN-501 monotherapy versus placebo.
efficacy_outcome: Week-12 MRI-PDFF least-squares mean change was −15.4% with TERN-501 1 mg, −27.5% with 3 mg (P = 0.0036), and −44.8% with 6 mg (P < 0.0001), versus −4.0% with placebo.

primary_endpoint: Change in liver stiffness on MRE at 6 or 12 months.
efficacy_outcome: MRE stiffness change (kPa): at 6 months, spironolactone 0.025 vs placebo −0.265; at 12 months, spironolactone 0.105 vs placebo 0.135. No statistical comparison reported.
safety_signal: Serious AEs: 0/11 with spironolactone and 0/6 with placebo; no deaths in either group.

efficacy_outcome: Across 21 RCTs (1,037 patients), probiotic intervention significantly reduced liver function, lipid, blood glucose, and insulin measures and improved hepatic steatosis; BMI, inflammatory factors, and HOMA-IR did not significantly improve. ALT, GGT, triglycerides, and blood glucose improved more with treatment lasting ≥12 weeks.

mechanism_of_action: Bivalent fibroblast growth factor 21 analogue.
primary_endpoint: Improvement in liver fibrosis (decrease ≥1 stage) without worsening of MASH at week 24; week-96 evaluation also reported.
efficacy_outcome: At week 96, fibrosis improvement without MASH worsening occurred in 19% with placebo, 30% with efruxifermin 28 mg (difference 12 percentage points; p=0.19), and 49% with 50 mg (difference 31 percentage points; p=0.0030).
safety_signal: Adverse events were reported by 95% (28 mg), 100% (50 mg), and 98% (placebo); mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal events were more common with efruxifermin. No drug-induced liver injury or deaths were reported.

mechanism_of_action: Cilofexor is a farnesoid X receptor agonist; firsocostat is an acetyl-CoA carboxylase inhibitor. Mechanisms for icosapent ethyl and fenofibrate are not stated.
efficacy_outcome: At 6 weeks of combination treatment, median triglyceride change was +41 mg/dL with icosapent ethyl and −2 mg/dL with fenofibrate; in the fenofibrate group, the within-group change was not significant (P = .92), while the icosapent ethyl group increased (P < .001).
safety_signal: Treatments were well tolerated; most treatment-emergent adverse events were Grade 1–2, with no discontinuations due to adverse events.

primary_endpoint: Percent change from baseline in fasting triglycerides at Week 27 for Cohort A and Week 25 for Cohorts B and C.
efficacy_outcome: Fasting triglycerides changed by −16% with pooled placebo, −36% with ISIS 703802 40 mg Q4W (p=0.0343), −53% with 80 mg Q4W (p<0.0001), and −47% with 20 mg QW (p=0.0009).
safety_signal: Serious adverse events: placebo 1/27; 40 mg Q4W 1/26; 80 mg Q4W 2/26; 20 mg QW 1/26. No deaths were reported.

primary_endpoint: Change in serum alanine transaminase level at 24 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Semaglutide reduced serum alanine transaminase (mean difference 14.07 U/L; 95% CI 19.39 to -8.75; p<0.001).
safety_signal: Serious adverse events were more frequent versus placebo (RR 1.54; 95% CI 1.02–2.34; p=0.04); common events included gastrointestinal and gallbladder-related disorders.

mechanism_of_action: Monoclonal antibody that binds beta-klotho and selectively activates the FGFR1c/beta-klotho co-receptor complex.
primary_endpoint: MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis by histology at Week 52.
efficacy_outcome: At Week 24, relative liver fat content reductions versus placebo were 19.1% with 50 mg, 19.0% with 100 mg, and 26.1% with 300 mg. Interim differences from placebo were deemed insufficient to continue the trial.
safety_signal: MK-3655 was generally well tolerated; no specific adverse events or rates were reported.

primary_endpoint: Gut microbiota composition after the 8.6-month intervention.
safety_signal: No adverse effects were observed with the interventions.

primary_endpoint: Histological features on liver biopsy at baseline and week 24.
Change from baseline liver fat content at 6 months.
Pooled incidence of ultrasound-diagnosed NAFLD in adults without NAFLD at baseline.

efficacy_outcome: After 6 months, the NAC/RSV group had reductions in steatosis (16.49%, P=0.001) and fibrosis (approximately 19.5%, P=0.001); the vitamin E group had a 6.05% reduction in steatosis (P=0.017).

mechanism_of_action: Tofogliflozin is a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor.
primary_endpoint: At 48 weeks, percentage of participants with at least a 1-point improvement in each histological score for steatosis, hepatocellular ballooning, lobular inflammation, and fibrosis.
efficacy_outcome: Tofogliflozin-group scores improved for fibrosis (60%, P=0.001), steatosis (65%, P=0.001), ballooning (55%, P=0.002), and lobular inflammation (50%, P=0.003); glimepiride improved ballooning (25%, P=0.025). Between-group change in fibrosis was not significant (P=0.172); the primary endpoint result was not reported.

primary_endpoint: ALT and body weight at 12 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: ALT change was −19.6 U/L with metronidazole followed by inulin versus −0.2 U/L with placebo-placebo (p=0.026); weight-loss maintenance did not differ.

primary_endpoint: Change in intrahepatic fat content measured by MRI-PDFF at 48 weeks compared with baseline.
Difference between initial and final liver triglyceride concentration measured by NMRS, comparing Aramchol with placebo at 3 months.
Improvement in hepatic histology; timepoint not stated.
efficacy_outcome: The primary outcome was achieved by 29.3% with vitamin E and 14.1% with placebo. Significant improvements in steatosis, lobular inflammation, and fibrosis stages were also reported in the vitamin E group.
safety_signal: 12 serious adverse events were reported; none were considered treatment-related.

primary_endpoint: Prevalence of metabolic syndrome and NAFLD among premenopausal and postmenopausal women.
Liver fat content at 2 weeks.

mechanism_of_action: The source states that bariatric surgery results in long-term weight loss and improves metabolic syndrome; it does not specify a mechanism of action.
primary_endpoint: Future cancer incidence after bariatric surgery (timepoint not specified).
efficacy_outcome: Bariatric surgery was associated with lower overall cancer incidence (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.46–0.84; p<0.002) and cancer-associated mortality (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.42–0.62; p<0.00001) versus conventional treatment.

After 8 weeks, NAFLD regressed in 52% of patients (P<0.05); visceral abdominal fat decreased 9%, body weight 1.4%, total cholesterol 2.5%, non-HDL cholesterol 3.2%, and circulating free fatty acids 8%.

mechanism_of_action: Pan-peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonist.
efficacy_outcome: Serum biomarker signatures identified histologic responders with AUC 0.81 ± 0.08 for E1, 0.80 ± 0.08 for E2, and 0.81 ± 0.08 for E3.

primary_endpoint: Overall survival (OS).
efficacy_outcome: After IPTW adjustment, atezolizumab plus bevacizumab showed no OS advantage over lenvatinib (HR 0.97; p=0.739).

primary_endpoint: Safety outcome and percentage of hepatic fat fraction at 24 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Hepatic fat fraction changed by −1.55, −0.90, and −1.85 percentage points in Treatment Arms A, B, and C, respectively; statistical comparisons were not reported.
safety_signal: Adverse events affected 17 participants with IMM-124E 600 mg, 14 with 1200 mg, and 13 with placebo. Serious AEs affected 1/43, 2/46, and 3/44, respectively; there were no deaths in the IMM-124E groups and one with placebo.

primary_endpoint: Improved metabolic parameters (glucose, lipids, liver enzymes, etc.) at 16 weeks.

efficacy_outcome: Across 26 RCTs (2,375 patients), silymarin improved several measures, including ALT (SMD −12.39, 95% CI −19.69 to −5.08), AST (SMD −10.97, 95% CI −15.51 to −6.43), and hepatic steatosis (OR 3.25, 95% CI 1.80–5.87). HOMA-IR was not significantly changed (SMD −0.37, 95% CI −0.77 to 0.04).

primary_endpoint: No primary endpoint specified; hepatic steatosis, metabolic measures, inflammatory biomarkers, and fibrosis were evaluated over 12 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Compared with control, all three intervention groups had significant decreases in alanine aminotransferase, insulin-resistance and insulin-sensitivity indices, fasting glucose, and fatty liver index (Bonferroni-adjusted p<0.008).

primary_endpoint: Intrahepatic lipid content assessed by MRI proton density fat fraction at 12 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Liver fat content was significantly lower after 12 weeks in the flaxseed group than before intervention (P < 0.05); no between-group result for the primary endpoint was specified.

mechanism_of_action: Proposed to ameliorate NAFLD by regulating the FGF21-adiponectin axis.
efficacy_outcome: After 3 months, fish oil versus corn oil significantly reduced serum ALT (net change −5.4 ± 14.5 vs −0.25 ± 4.70 U/L; P=0.001) and triacylglycerol (−0.70 ± 1.10 vs 0.11 ± 1.04 mmol/L; P=0.018), decreased FGF21, and increased adiponectin.

primary_endpoint: Percent change from baseline in hepatic fat fraction by MRI-PDFF at Week 12.
efficacy_outcome: At Week 12, hepatic fat fraction changed by -32.9% with MGL-3196 versus -10.4% with placebo (p<0.0001).
safety_signal: Serious AEs occurred in 5/84 participants receiving MGL-3196 and 2/41 receiving placebo in the main study; no deaths in either group. Extension study: 0/31 serious AEs and no deaths.

primary_endpoint: Incidence of adverse events with once-daily oral resmetirom 80 or 100 mg versus placebo at 52 weeks.

mechanism_of_action: Bivalent fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) analogue.
primary_endpoint: Reduction of at least one fibrosis stage without worsening of MASH at week 36.
efficacy_outcome: At week 36, the endpoint occurred in 18% with efruxifermin 28 mg versus 13% with placebo (adjusted difference 3 percentage points; 95% CI, −11 to 17; P=0.62) and in 19% with 50 mg versus 13% with placebo (difference 4 percentage points; 95% CI, −10 to 18; P=0.52).
safety_signal: Gastrointestinal adverse events were more common with efruxifermin; most were mild or moderate.

primary_endpoint: Not specified in the abstract; NAFLD was assessed by liver biopsy.
efficacy_outcome: No statistically significant between-group changes in NAFLD. Compared with HCLF, LCHF improved HbA1c more (difference in change −6.1 mmol/mol; 95% CI −9.2 to −3.0) and reduced weight more (−3.8 kg; 95% CI −6.2 to −1.4); changes were not sustained at 9 months.

mechanism_of_action: Non-steroidal farnesoid X receptor (FXR) agonist; FXR is described as a regulator of bile acid, glucose, and lipid homeostasis.
efficacy_outcome: After 4 weeks, ALT (p=0.027) and GGT (p=0.019) decreased, and insulin sensitivity improved in 92% of patients (p=0.02); hepatic steatosis measures did not change.
safety_signal: No serious adverse events; short intervals of cardiac arrhythmia in 2 patients led to study termination.

efficacy_outcome: At 12 weeks, the high-protein diet plus beta-cryptoxanthin group had greater reductions than control in ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, and GGT (mean differences −27.2, −7.2, −39.2, and −16.3 IU/L; all p<0.010). Grade 0 steatosis remission was 82.6% versus 0.0% in control (p<0.001).
safety_signal: Sixteen patients reported minor adverse events; event details were not reported.

primary_endpoint: Liver fat content at 8 weeks (6 weeks post-treatment).
efficacy_outcome: Liver fat content decreased from 8.38 to 7.72 with H. pylori eradication and from 8.50 to 7.29 with lifestyle modification; between-group p=0.10. Within-group changes were significant (both p<0.01).
safety_signal: Serious adverse events: 0/20 in the H. pylori eradication group and 0/20 in the no-intervention group; deaths not reported.

primary_endpoint: Change in hepatic fat by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) from baseline at 12 weeks.

mechanism_of_action: A polyethylene glycol-conjugated analog of human fibroblast growth factor 21, a nonmitogenic hormone that regulates energy metabolism.
primary_endpoint: At week 48, improvement of ≥1 stage in the NASH Clinical Research Network fibrosis score without NASH worsening.
efficacy_outcome: Primary endpoint responses occurred in 24%–28% of pegbelfermin arms versus 31% with placebo (P = .361).
safety_signal: Serious adverse events were more frequent with pegbelfermin than placebo, though none were treatment related. One patient receiving 40 mg discontinued because of worsening ascites.

mechanism_of_action: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
primary_endpoint: MASH improvement without worsening of liver fibrosis at 48 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Primary endpoint occurred in 53% (41/78) with dapagliflozin vs 30% (23/76) with placebo (risk ratio 1.73, 95% CI 1.16–2.58; P=0.006).
safety_signal: Discontinuation because of adverse events occurred in 1% (1/78) with dapagliflozin and 3% (2/76) with placebo.

mechanism_of_action: Improves insulin sensitivity and promotes weight loss; increased hepatic de novo lipogenesis and unchanged fatty acid oxidation partly explain the lack of improvement in intrahepatic triglyceride content.
primary_endpoint: Change in intrahepatic triglyceride content after 12 weeks of metformin treatment.
efficacy_outcome: After 12 weeks, intrahepatic triglyceride content and fatty acid oxidation remained unchanged; body weight decreased and insulin sensitivity improved. VLDL-triglyceride concentrations decreased, while the relative contribution of de novo lipogenesis-derived fatty acids to VLDL-triglyceride increased.

primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in mGFRiohexol and eGFRcreatinine at week 16.
Participants with improvement in NAFLD activity by standardized liver biopsy scoring from baseline to 96 weeks.
efficacy_outcome: Improvement occurred in 27 participants on pioglitazone, 36 on vitamin E, and 16 on placebo; reported Mantel-Haenszel p-values were 0.001 and 0.04.
safety_signal: Serious adverse events affected 2/80 participants on pioglitazone, 7/84 on vitamin E, and 10/83 on placebo; deaths were not reported.

primary_endpoint: Change in AST to Platelet Ratio Index (APRI) score after 6 months.
efficacy_outcome: APRI decreased over time in the probiotic group; no numerical estimate or p-value was reported. Liver fibrosis, steatosis, and inflammatory activity showed no significant between-group differences.

mechanism_of_action: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist.
primary_endpoint: At week 72: resolution of steatohepatitis without worsening of liver fibrosis, and reduction in liver fibrosis without worsening of steatohepatitis.
efficacy_outcome: Resolution without worsening of fibrosis: 62.9% with semaglutide vs 34.3% with placebo (difference 28.7 percentage points; P<0.001). Fibrosis reduction without worsening of steatohepatitis: 36.8% vs 22.4% (difference 14.4 percentage points; P<0.001).
safety_signal: Gastrointestinal adverse events were more common with semaglutide.

primary_endpoint: At 24 weeks, ≥30% reduction in MRI-PDFF.
efficacy_outcome: Primary endpoint achieved by 20% with oligonol vs 15% with placebo (p=0.50); MRI-PDFF change was not different between groups.

primary_endpoint: Percentage achieving ≥1-stage fibrosis improvement without worsening NASH at Week 72.
efficacy_outcome: At Week 72, 13.7% with SEMA + CILO/FIR FDC versus 8.3% with matched placebo; p=0.2289.
safety_signal: Serious AEs: 17/124 with SEMA + CILO/FIR FDC; 13/122 with SEMA + PTM CILO/FIR; 18/123 with PTM SEMA + CILO/FIR FDC; and 11/84 with both PTM treatments. Deaths: 0, 1, 1, and 0, respectively.

drugs.name: DT-enabled personalized nutrition, activity, and sleep

mechanism_of_action: Digital twin technology predicts postprandial glycemic responses to personalize nutrition, activity, and sleep; the source states postprandial hyperglycemia drives insulin resistance and inflammation.
primary_endpoint: Change in HbA1c and medicine reduction between groups at 1 year.
efficacy_outcome: At 1 year, HbA1c decreased by 2.9 (SD 1.8) with DT versus 0.3 (SD 1.2) with standard care (P < .001); T2D remission with DT was 72.7%. In participants with abnormal baseline values, NAFLD liver fat score changed by −2.5 (SD 2.0) versus −0.1 (SD 1.5), and NAFLD fibrosis score by −1.20 (SD 0.9) versus −0.1 (SD 1.0), both P < .001.

primary_endpoint: Change in ALT level at 24 weeks.

mechanism_of_action: GLP-1 receptor agonists
efficacy_outcome: Histologic resolution of NASH without worsening liver fibrosis was significantly improved (2 RCTs; WMD 4.08, 95% CI 2.54–6.56; p < 0.00001). CRP was also reduced (7 RCTs; WMD −0.41, 95% CI −0.78 to −0.04; p = 0.002).

mechanism_of_action: Cyclophilin inhibitor.
primary_endpoint: Relative bioavailability of a single 225-mg dose under fasted versus high-fat fed conditions.
safety_signal: No treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in the fasted group; 1 occurred in the high-fat meal group.

primary_endpoint: Liver ultrasound view (gradient change), assessed before intervention and 48 hours after its end; other listed co-primary outcomes include BMI, lipid levels, and liver enzymes at the same timepoints.
Participants with treatment-emergent adverse events possibly or probably related to treatment, from first dose through Day 113 (±5 days).
safety_signal: Possibly/probably treatment-related TEAEs occurred in 0 participants at 25 mg, 0 at 50 mg, 1 at 100 mg, and 3 at 200 mg in cohorts 1–4; pooled placebo had 0. Serious AEs occurred in 1/6 participants in the 200 mg cohort 4b and none in the other reported groups; no deaths were reported.

mechanism_of_action: Dasatinib and quercetin are described as senolytics that target senescent cells.
primary_endpoint: Adverse events and study feasibility over the 3-week dosing period.
safety_signal: No serious adverse events related to dasatinib and quercetin were reported. Sleep disturbances and anxiety occurred in 4/6 participants receiving dasatinib and quercetin versus 0/6 receiving placebo.

primary_endpoint: Association between primary hypothyroidism and MASLD prevalence and severity.

mechanism_of_action: FMT was reported to improve gut microbiota dysbiosis.
Acts as a free radical scavenger and modulates enzymes associated with cellular damage, fibrosis, and cirrhosis.
safety_signal: Generally well tolerated, with a low incidence of adverse events; no treatment-related serious adverse events or deaths were reported in clinical trials.

mechanism_of_action: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist.
primary_endpoint: At 72 weeks, resolution of NASH with no worsening of fibrosis.
efficacy_outcome: NASH resolution without worsening fibrosis occurred in 40%, 36%, and 59% with semaglutide 0.1, 0.2, and 0.4 mg, respectively, versus 17% with placebo; for 0.4 mg versus placebo, P<0.001.
safety_signal: With semaglutide 0.4 mg versus placebo, nausea occurred in 42% vs. 11%, constipation in 22% vs. 12%, and vomiting in 15% vs. 2%. Malignant neoplasms occurred in 3 semaglutide-treated patients (1%) and no placebo-treated patients.

primary_endpoint: Incidence of adverse events with once-daily oral resmetirom at 52 weeks.
Change in intrahepatic triglyceride content measured by MRI at 12 months.
efficacy_outcome: At 12 months, IHTG decreased 6.9% with TRE and 7.9% with DCR; between-group difference 1.0 percentage point (95% CI, −1.6 to 3.5; P = .45).

mechanism_of_action: PDE4 inhibitor
primary_endpoint: ALT at 12 weeks

mechanism_of_action: The authors attributed DSSG effects to increased superoxide dismutase activity and reduced malondialdehyde and NF-κB activity in a rat NAFLD model.
efficacy_outcome: In patients, DSSG had significantly highest effects on ultrasound findings and reductions in total cholesterol, triglycerides, AST, and GGT; Silibinin had the highest ALT reduction and rosiglitazone the highest fasting glucose reduction. In rats, DSSG significantly reduced glucose, lipids, liver enzymes, and NF-κB expression versus untreated NAFLD animals (P < 0.001).

mechanism_of_action: Oral pan-caspase inhibitor.
primary_endpoint: Change in hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) at week 24.
efficacy_outcome: No significant difference in change in HVPG versus placebo for any dose; adjusted differences were −0.21, −0.45, and −0.58 mmHg for 5, 25, and 50 mg, respectively.
safety_signal: New or worsening decompensating events occurred in approximately 10% over median exposure of 337 days; events and treatment-emergent adverse events were similar across groups. Emricasan appeared safe and well tolerated.

primary_endpoint: Liver histological improvement at 48 weeks.
Steatosis histology at baseline and 12 months.

mechanism_of_action: Dual glucagon-like peptide 1 and glucagon receptor agonist.
primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in postprandial hepatic glycogen at day 28 (part A) and fasting hepatic glycogen at day 35 (part B), with cotadutide versus placebo.
Changes in MRI-PDFF and histologic features of MASH after bariatric intervention.
efficacy_outcome: MRI-PDFF showed a 72% reduction at 6 months (ratio of means, 0.28); NAS decreased by 60% at 3–6 months, 40% at 12–24 months, and 50% at 36–60 months. Histologic features also improved, including significant fibrosis (≥F2), reduced by 18% at 12–24 months and 17% at 36–60 months.

primary_endpoint: Histological improvement in NASH, including fibrosis improvement.
efficacy_outcome: OCA improved NASH fibrosis versus control (OR 1.95, 95% CI 1.47–2.59; p<0.001); results were significant for 10 mg (OR 1.61; p=0.03) and 25 mg (OR 2.23; p<0.001).
safety_signal: In NASH, 25 mg OCA increased adverse events leading to discontinuation (OR 2.8; p<0.001), while 10 mg did not (OR 0.95; p=0.84). Pruritus risk was lowest with 5 mg OCA.

primary_endpoint: Normalization or >50% reduction in serum ALT from baseline at 6 months.
efficacy_outcome: 7 subjects were reported as improved at 6 months; no comparator or statistical significance was reported.
safety_signal: No serious adverse events among 13 subjects; deaths not reported.

mechanism_of_action: Bivalent Fc-FGF21 analogue that replicates FGF21 agonism of fibroblast growth factor receptor 1c, 2c, or 3c.
primary_endpoint: Proportion with at least 1-stage fibrosis improvement and no worsening of NASH at week 24.
efficacy_outcome: In the liver biopsy analysis set, endpoint achieved by 39% (15/38) with efruxifermin 28 mg (RR 2.3, 95% CI 1.1–4.8; p=0.025) and 41% (14/34) with 50 mg (RR 2.2, 95% CI 1.0–5.0; p=0.036), versus 20% (8/41) with placebo. In the full analysis set, rates were 36% vs 19% for 28 mg (p=0.033) and 33% vs 19% for 50 mg (p=0.123).
safety_signal: Diarrhoea occurred in 40% of each efruxifermin group versus 19% with placebo; nausea in 28% and 42% versus 23%, respectively, mostly grade 1–2. Five patients discontinued due to adverse events; four serious adverse events occurred in the 50 mg group, one considered drug related; no deaths.

primary_endpoint: Change in liver stiffness measurement and ultrasound score from baseline to week 12.

mechanism_of_action: Inappropriate diets may promote MASLD and abdominal obesity through hepatic de novo lipid synthesis, insulin resistance, gut-liver dysfunction, and inflammation. Visceral fat increases free-fatty-acid flux to the liver, contributing to oxidative and endoplasmic-reticulum stress, PKC-pathway activation, and inflammation.

primary_endpoint: Liver fat content (LFC), measured by magnetic resonance spectroscopy or liver biopsy/NAS.
efficacy_outcome: LFC decreased with pioglitazone (−8.0 ± 1.0%, p < 0.001), diet and exercise (−7.8 ± 1.7%, p < 0.001), and omega-3 fatty acids (−6.0 ± 2.5%, p = 0.02).

primary_endpoint: Blood-brain barrier permeability measured by MRI on post-bleed day 5.
Number of participants with a 30% reduction in ALT from baseline at 12 months.
efficacy_outcome: 19 participants with pentoxifylline vs 7 with placebo; p=0.46 (ANOVA).
safety_signal: Serious adverse events: 0/19 with pentoxifylline and 0/7 with placebo; deaths not reported.

mechanism_of_action: MPC inhibition was linked to activation of mTOR and AMPK signaling, reduced BCKDH phosphorylation, and increased BCAA catabolism.
efficacy_outcome: In patients with NASH, plasma BCAA concentrations decreased from baseline with MSDC-0602K, while placebo had no effect; numerical results were not reported.

primary_endpoint: Changes in ALT, AST, and GGT in NAFLD patients according to statin treatment; no primary endpoint was specified.
efficacy_outcome: In interventional studies, ALT decreased by 27.2 U/L (35.41%), AST by 18.82 U/L (31.78%), and GGT by 19.93 U/L (25.57%). Cross-sectional studies found no difference in AST or GGT between statin-treated and untreated patients.

primary_endpoint: Safety through follow-up to week 26.
efficacy_outcome: No significant difference in adverse events between FMT and placebo; no significant change in mean BMI at week 12 in either group.
safety_signal: No significant differences in adverse events between FMT and placebo; FMT capsules were well tolerated.

primary_endpoint: Fibrosis improvement ≥1 stage without worsening of steatohepatitis and steatohepatitis resolution without worsening of fibrosis, both at Week 52; time to first disease progression up to 5 years.

drugs.name: Linzhi Jianghuang Fufang Huoxue Anshen Capsule (LJF)

primary_endpoint: MRI-PDFF at Week 24 (baseline Week 0).

mechanism_of_action: Engineered analog of the human hormone FGF19.
primary_endpoint: Change in Enhanced Liver Fibrosis from baseline to week 48.
efficacy_outcome: At week 48, the 3 mg group had a least-squares mean difference in ELF change of −0.5 versus placebo (95% CI −0.7 to −0.2; p=0.0003).
safety_signal: Diarrhea occurred in 26% and 40% of the 1 mg and 3 mg groups, respectively, versus 18% with placebo. Treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation in 2% and 9% of the 1 mg and 3 mg groups, respectively, versus 0% with placebo.

mechanism_of_action: Precise mechanism remains elusive; proposed receptors include CB1, CB2, PPARs, GPR55, and TRP channels.

primary_endpoint: Efficacy on glycaemic control parameters at baseline and week 16.
Percentage change from baseline in liver fat content assessed by MRI-PDFF at day 61.
efficacy_outcome: At day 61, liver fat change was -26.8% with HU6 150 mg, -35.6% with 300 mg, and -33.0% with 450 mg, versus +5.4% with placebo; statistical significance was not reported.
safety_signal: No serious adverse events or deaths were reported: 0/20, 0/21, and 0/19 with HU6 150, 300, and 450 mg, respectively, and 0/20 with placebo.

primary_endpoint: Not stated; assessed one-year changes in gut microbiota in relation to changes in HSI and FIB-4.
efficacy_outcome: Gut microbiota changes were associated with changes in HSI and FIB-4. Reported differences included lower Akkermansia and higher Desulfovibrio in FIB-4 change T1, and lower Enterobacteriaceae with higher Sutterella, Faecalibacterium, and Blautia in T3; no quantitative treatment-effect comparison was reported.

drugs.name: C-C motif chemokine receptor 2 and receptor 5 antagonists
lifestyle changes to achieve weight loss

mechanism_of_action: Mechanisms under investigation include farnesoid X nuclear receptor agonism, C-C motif chemokine receptor 2 and receptor 5 antagonism, stearoyl-CoA desaturase-1, and thyroid hormone receptor beta agonism.

efficacy_outcome: Vitamin E significantly decreased LDL and total cholesterol; most other measures, including liver enzymes and histology, showed no significant change (P>0.05). NAS had P<0.05, but the evidence was considered insufficient. Fasting glucose significantly increased with interventions lasting ≤12 months.
safety_signal: Fasting glucose significantly increased with interventions lasting ≤12 months.

primary_endpoint: Fibroscan, soluble vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (Svcam-1), adiponectin, and leptin at 6 months.

mechanism_of_action: Sulforaphane increased Bacteroides and Lactobacillus, promoting SCFA production and GPR41/43 activation, which increased GLP-1; it also protected the intestinal mucosal barrier and reduced inflammation.
efficacy_outcome: In the human NAFLD intervention, GLP-1 increased and was positively correlated with reductions in blood glucose and HOMA-IR; no numerical results were reported. In HFD-fed rats, SFN reduced blood glucose and HOMA-IRI and increased insulin sensitivity.
